lines.english: "Ah…"
"I just left the library."
"The weather outside is nice today, so I'll come back home after a little stroll."
"By the way, I'll be able to return to work soon."
"The monthly managerial meeting will be held at the end of this week, and I'm thinking of showing up then."
"Thank you for everything until now, Setsuna. I'm sorry for burdening you so much when you already had your hands full with work."
"You don't have to come every week anymore. Spend this weekend at your own place, and rest."
"Haruki-kun…"
Spring has passed, and summer has begun, at least according to the calendar.
The mornings and evenings are still chilly, but the days are just as cheerfully warm as I remember.
"Good work, but don't push yourself too hard. Use a taxi instead if it becomes too hard on you."
Haruki-kun has started his rehabilitation.
He's been consulting a doctor and he's getting better, little by little.
For now, he'll be going to the library during the day once a week, allowing him to get in touch with people and society in a quiet atmosphere.
Hearing that makes me happy of course, but the greatest news is this.
"But I guess I understand why you'd want to go for a stroll today. The air feels amazing, doesn't it?"
Haruki-kun sent me a text.
He didn't even charge his cell phone until very recently. Even now, he never calls me nor answers any of my calls.
But even so, he's begun to talk about himself to meーand only meーagain. That's the thing I'm the happiest about.
"Ah, I'm on my way back to the office by the way. It's not like I'm texting at work or anything."
Since a long time ago, his texts have been something for me to lean on.
There were days when I'd wait impatiently for the one text a day he'd send me.
The promise was that he'd only text me once a day, yet I kept waiting for the second, and then the third…
"…But I guess it's kinda unclear whether texting while on the move from one post to another counts as slacking off at work. Hehe."
When we lost sight of each other, when I ended up rejecting him, and when our bond was so terribly damaged…
During those times, it was those single texts that would once again bind us together.
"Back on topic though. So you're thinking about going back to work, huh. That's amazing! Looks like you've gotten a lot better."
"But you don't have to be in such a rush. I've told you this before, but you should go through the steps slowly, but steadily."
"Let's discuss everything together, okay? Like the managerial meeting, your medicine, and the state of your workplace."
"With that in mind, I think I'll head over this weekend as well. There's so much to talk about now, after all."
"In fact, I'd be really glad if you didn't try to take away the one thing I'm looking forward to so much. I'll go there no matter what!"
"Goodbye."
"The weekend, huh."
But…
I'm happy, of course, but I can't let myself be immersed in my own sense of satisfaction.
His text just now really seemed optimistic. I could feel the will behind what he told me.
But that's precisely why I feel so uneasy. I really hope this is just me overthinking it, but…
Going back to work all of a sudden… It's far too early to make that kind of judgment.
That's a decision he should make with a calm mind, with the advice of those around him.
Besides, this weekend is…
"Now onto the weekend weather report."
"In the afternoon tomorrow, the humid weather in the west will carry over here."
"Just like in Kyushu and Shikoku, everywhere from Kinki to Kanto will be experiencing a rainy season starting this weekend."
"I'm back…"
And then, on Friday…
"Haruki-kun?"
As usual, I could feel the presence of someone in this closed off, dark room.
But unlike before, that presence was not on the bed…
"I said you didn't have to come."
But rather in the corner of the room directly opposite it.
Leaning against the wall, looking up at nothing in particular, muttering some words with even less energy than usual.
"How did the meeting go?"
"…I didn't go."
"I see."
"The rain… The rain wouldn't stop, so…"
"Yup, you did the right thing. I'm glad you didn't go. I mean look at me, I'm all drenched…"
"Damn it, why does it have to rain? On such an important day…!"
Everything stands in contrast to the text he sent me yesterdayーhis tone, his voice, and his words.
The way Haruki-kun is now, the slightest trigger can send his emotions into disarray.
"Nothing we can do about the weather. Another day, perhaps."
I sit beside him, but I make sure to maintain a small distance so I don't get him wet.
Then on top of that, I maintain a bit more distance, so that I don't scare him… so that I don't make him feel suffocated.
"But I didn't go to the last meeting either. This makes it the second month I haven't shown up for work."
"Like I said, there's no need to rush. You always have to be so hasty, Haruki-kun."
I softly put my hand on his shoulder, guessing that this small amount of physical contact won't make him reject me.
Our level of intimacy changes by the day, so like always, I have to feel my way around to figure out what degree is okay.
"At this rate I'll be forgotten by everyone. It'll be as if I was never there from the start."
"Of course that won't happen. Everyone is waiting for you."
"How could you possibly know that? What would you know about my workplace, Setsuna…"
"Well, you know… my job is kinda similar."
"Must be nice, Setsuna… always being so busy."
"I'm just slow at my job, that's all. All I ever do is cause trouble for my co-workers."
"Must be nice being needed by everyone."
"I keep telling you, you're needed as well. They even sent you a postcard with everyone's names on it."
Beside his bed lies a piece of colored paper, sent by the editorial staff of Kaiousha.
From what I heard, the whole thing was planned by a former superior of his who now lives in America.
"That's just… how everyone felt about me two months ago, when they thought I'd get better in no time."
"No one thought that. Everyone just hopes that you'll get better someday."
That's how important he is to the company he works for.
"You can't know how anyone there is feeling right now… No, they probably don't even care anymore."
He's merely the only one who can't bring himself to believe that.
"They'll wait for you… You were good enough at your job for them to wait patiently now. I'm certain they'll wait for you."
"How would you know? People's feelings change all the time…"
"No, they don't."
"Yes, they do. After two years spent together with you, I…"
The words that Haruki-kun couldn't help spilling out cause me the slightest hint of pain.
But that inflicted pain is far from what he intended with those words.
"I betrayed you, Setsuna, when I was supposed to love you forever…"
And that's the reason.
That's the reason I can find it in myself to believe. That unchanging feelings do exist. That love that never fizzles out does exist.
I had no choice but to believe it, when I had to sit beside you for five years as you kept thinking about Kazusa.
"It still makes no sense to me… How can you bring yourself to stay by my side, Setsuna…?"
"I told you, I'm doing this because I want to…"
"I know I told you… that I couldn't live without you, Setsuna…"
"You did…?"
"But that doesn't mean you should remain with someone like me. If I can't live without you, then I should just die."
"Haruki-kun… stop it. You can't ever say that, even as a joke…"
"I should just die already…! I need to set you free, Setsuna…!"
"I'm sorry, I'm sorry… I'm so sorry for making you suffer so much."
"Don't apologize… It only makes me feel more pathetic…!"
"Haruki-kun…"
His shivering body looks more feeble than ever.
I want to hug this feeble body with every fiber of my being. I want to ease his terrible suffering, even if only a little bit.
But I can't do that right now.
Because to him, my hug is probably nothing more than the painful embrace of a vine full of thorns.
Spring has passed, and summer has begun, at least according to the calendar.
And…
Along with the heat, this season of gloomy dimness begins.
I wake up to an all too familiar ceiling.
The ceiling of the apartment I used to visit every weekend for two years, it is not. It's the ceiling I've been looking up at since I was born, in my own room.
After turning off the alarm and opening the window, I'm greeted by the same dreary sky as yesterday.
Rain once again…
"Mh…"
A weekend morning, spent apart from Haruki-kun.
Yes, in the end I didn't stay at his place.
Yesterday, he was in such a terrible state that just having me around was enough to ruin him, something that only happens once every two weeks or so.
The sound of the rain and the darkness of the sky seeped into the tepidness of his room, robbing him of any courage or joy he had left.
On days like that, I never managed to restore Haruki-kun's strength, no matter how much I tried to console him, encourage him, or embrace him.
That's why I did the only thing I could to put his mind at ease a little… by disappearing from his sight.
"I have to wake up…"
Every weekend morning, I'm always caught in a struggle between myself and my low blood pressure, which keeps trying to hold me tied down to bed.
"I have to go…"
So that I can spend time with Haruki-kun.
Did he get any sleep after that, I wonder? Did he regain some strength, I wonder?
Did he eat properly, I wonder?
I need to make sure, because sometimes he'll even go days without drinking a single drop of water if I don't keep my eyes on him.
With my thoughts thoroughly occupied with those worries, I grab hold of my pajamas and begin to change.
"…Huh?"
I felt a strange sense of disgust at the words that had just left my mouth.
What did I mean by "I have to go"?
"Okay, I'm heading out now."
"Ah, Setsuna, what about dinner today?"
Whenever I leave on the weekends, I never tell them where I'm going.
And they've never bothered asking either.
"Don't need any. I'll eat over there."
"…Will you return home today?"
There aren't enough options for that to be a question worth asking.
"…I don't know. I'll call you in any case."
"I see… Be careful not to slip in the rain, okay?"
"Yeah, I know. Okay then, see you."
This has been the unwritten rule in this household for the past two years.
Until half a year ago, they'd let it slide with a bitter smile; now, it's with a sigh.
"Wait a minute, Setsuna."
"Dad…"
But not today…
"I need to have a talk with you, along with your mother."
"Sorry, but I'm in a hurry right now. How about tonight or tomorrow night instead?"
"No, it has to be right now. I won't allow you to leave this house until we've had a talk."
"Honey…"
"Do you mean…"
On that ever so stagnant everyday life of mine, a chilly and damp breeze flows in.
Just like the weather outside.
"Are you telling me to stop going? Are you telling me to abandon him!?"
"I haven't said that at all. Stop purposefully interpreting things in the most extreme way."
"You're the one being extreme, Dad!"
He told me not to go. He told me to keep my distance from him.
I always felt like those words were on the tip of his tongue these past weeks, and now he finally said it.
Further still, I'm surrounded by the chilly wind.
"Haruki-kun is family now, you know? How can you be so heartless to him just because he fell a bit ill!? You're cruel!"
"He has a family of his own. Wouldn't asking them for help be the proper thing to do?"
Dad's asserting that his family should be the one responsible for his current problem.
"In fact, wouldn't you agree that not even asking his family for their opinion is the truly heartless thing here?"
"I already explained this a hundred times… Haruki-kun isn't on good terms with his mom…"
He's telling me to leave Haruki-kun in the care of someone he hasn't talked to in years…
"Yes, I've heard that many times from you, Setsuna, but I haven't heard any of the details from Kitahara-kun himself."
"Just talking about it is painful for him… There's no way he could handle the emotional stress, given the state he's in now."
I'm the only one he'll ever tell that story to. Myself and… one other person…
No, he told her first and only told me out of convenience. About the past he had cast away.
"Perhaps Kitahara-san's symptoms have something to do with his relationship to his family. Maybe that's the cause."
"If that's the case, all the more reason to help get rid of that cause. A talk with his family could very well be a start."
"But it could also be the start of something bad, couldn't it?"
Mom's small helping hand was easily waved away by my dad's forceful reasoning.
So in the end, I'm left struggling against him alone.
"Yes, maybe what you're saying is right, Dad, but it's all just words and lacks empathy."
"I assure you it's not just words. I'm also worried about Kitahara-kun."
"But then…!"
"That's why I'll do everything in my power… I'll meet with his family and have a talk with them."
"Honey, I'm not sure if that's…"
But Dad is far too strong today.
Instead of just being confidently correct like usual, he's willing to compromise and consider my feelings as well.
…Maybe he saw no other way to handle his daughter, who's every bit as stubborn as he is.
"He might simply be in a bad way because he lost sight of his family when he was younger. Shouldn't we at least ask his mother what she thinks?"
"Dad…"
Dad's suggestion is one I've thought about many times before.
"We can just set things straight if there was simply a misunderstanding between them.
"What do you mean, a lot?"
In other words, he's just as worried about him as I am.
"A lot means a lot. For one, it means trying to support him as a family, rather than putting the entire burden on you, Setsuna."
"What else?"
"The rest we'll figure out after having a proper talk with them. We need to properly think about what we'll do from here on out."
However…
Unlike me, my dad doesn't lose his way. He doesn't hesitate to put those ideas into action.
"Setsuna, we'll help you. Let's all work together on this. Now listen to me, don't get too absorbed in him."
"You're still only a second-year at your job. You should have your plate full just looking out for yourself."
What if Haruki-kun only gets worse when his family gets involved?
What if the talk doesn't go well, and the distance between our families only grows larger, regardless of what we want?
He doesn't have a shred of unease over those possibilities. "What if I'm wrong?" doesn't even enter his mind.
"Was that… everything? I'll be on my way then."
"Setsuna…"
If he makes the wrong decision and Haruki-kun… and our relationship breaks apart.
"I think you're correct, Dad… but correct is all you are."
He'll probably just call it "bad luck" or say that "it wasn't meant to be."
"If people's emotions could be swayed by logic, an illness like his wouldn't exist in the first place."
"But the way you're handling it isn't doing him any good."
"Yes it is! He'll get better! I'll make Haruki-kun return to his old self no matter what!"
I couldn't possibly accept an option so slow, deliberate and high-risk.
"Mom… you understand me, right?"
That's why, as unfair as it is, I try to defeat him through strength in numbers.
"Right, Mom? Have a bit more trust in me."
By dragging in my mom, who albeit reservedly, has taken my side until now.
"I think that… letting Setsuna do things her own way just a little bit longer… wouldn't be a problem."
"Mom…!"
And I hit the nail on the head.
"But Dear…"
"We still don't know if talking to his parents is what Kitahara-san wants."
"It's not possible right now. Haruki-kun can't make that kind of decision yet, and I don't want to force him to either."
"However, if he's to become part of our family, we need to get this out of the way sooner or later."
"I think… just this once, I disagree with you a little, Honey."
"What do you disagree on? Aren't you worried about Setsuna?"
"Of course, Setsuna's well-being is the most important thing for me too."
"Come on, I'm perfectly fine. Dad's just a worrywart."
"But what I'm trying to say is not that… I really don't want to be saying this, but…"
I thought I hit the nail on the head…
"If perhaps, something were to happen between them, and… they break up as a result…"
"M-Mom?"
That's why for a good few seconds, I didn't fully understand what Mom was trying to say.
"Then perhaps it'd be better if… we weren't on speaking terms with his family…"
"Dear…?"
"What are you saying, Mom!?"
It came as a complete shock.
I thought she was on my side. I thought she'd take my side over Dad's.
Yet the words my mom just uttered…
"Setsuna, listen to me. This is something worth thinking about even if Kitahara-san wasn't ill."
"Wait… a second."
She interrupted my dad's proposal, just like I wanted her to.
But it wasn't at all because she thought that I was right, or that Dad was wrong.
She simply had her own reason.
I'm afraid that something bad will happen if his family interferes.
But what she's worried about is the family ties we'll be stuck with after we break up.
"You're only 24, after all. A single failed relationship wouldn't prevent you from starting again with someon…"
"I won't ever fail! I'll never find someone new! I'll become happy with him and no one else!"
"Setsuna…"
My thoughts turn blank, my vision turns pitch black, and the back of my neck feels scorching hot.
"Why? Why would you say things like that now of all times, Mom!?"
The cold, sharp sting I'm feeling doesn't come from Dad's orders or warnings, but from Mom's support and advice.
"Nee-chan, wait up."
"Leave me alone! Mom put you up to this anyway, didn't she?"
"What, are you gonna walk into the pouring rain without an umbrella? Come on, take this with you."
The very moment I left the house in a fit of rage, the ceaseless rain mercilessly poured down on me.
Deeming it a lost cause, I thought about going back… Only then realizing that I had left in my slippers.
"You know… Mom's starting to notice."
"Notice what?"
I take the umbrella without looking him in the eye, and then proceed to pull out a pair of rain boots from the shoe rack.
"She's starting to wonder whether something bad happened between you and Kitahara-san.
I'm so glad our eyes aren't meeting. I'm so glad he can't see the expression on my face.
"She's beginning to wonder whether the true cause of Kitahara-san's illness is related to that…"
"…Not at all. Nothing bad happened, so it's not the cause."
"Really?"
"Of course… We've always been in love with each other. Past, present, and future!"
"…No point telling your little brother that. It just makes me feel uncomfortable."
"It's your fault for bringing it up."
I keep telling my family that there are no problems, so why do they insist on being so worried all the time?
"Hey, Nee-chan. Do you actually plan on marrying Kitahara-san?"
"Why do you have to say that now? First Mom, and now you, Takahiro…"
And why are they so intent on staying suspicious of everyone outside the family?
"Both of you! Until just recently, you both treated him like family, didn't you!?"
Until half a year ago, he was unquestionably a part of the family.
And that was such a joyous thing for him.
He used to tell me that when we were snuggling, with an embarrassed smile on his face.
"It's not like I hate him now or anything. But if things go on like this, Nee-chan, you'll…"
"I'll what?"
So why did things turn out like this…?
"It's okay… Haruki-kun will get better in no time. Everything will return to normal, both Haruki-kun and our family."
"But I haven't seen any change in the past four months."
"Things like these take time."
"Then you were lying when you said he'd get better in no time."
"…! Why do you have to grasp at straws like that!?"
"Ah no, I'm sorry. It's just that… I feel you're getting the short end of the stick here, Nee-chan. I don't like how this is playing out."
"If you really think so, then you should stay quiet and support me. Isn't that what family is all about?"
"Maybe it is, but…"
"This is an important time for me right now. Mom and dad don't understand that at all."
Dad has demoted him from "family member" to "potential family member." Mom has started to entertain the thought of us breaking up.
"This is precisely the time I have to support him, and I need to do it slowly and carefully."
Am I the only one left still on Haruki-kun's side, I wonder?
"What is it? Was anything I said wrong?"
"I don't think it's wrong, but… Are you really okay with this, Nee-chan? The way you're describing it…"
"Describing it? What do you mean?"
"'I have to support him.' It sounds like you're doing it against your will."
"Up until now, you always said 'I want to support him.'"
"Eh, eeh…!?"
"I have to go…"
"I have to support him."
"I've got nothing to do with this, so I can't act like I know everything, but…"
What is it that I'm beginning to lose in my speech?
Is it strength? Happiness? Optimism?
"You're always super absorbed in Kitahara-san and everything, but be careful this time, okay? Don't let him drag you down."
"If you really think so, you could at least be more considerate about it! That goes for dad, mom, and you too, Takahiro!"
"…Sorry!"
"No, it's okay… I realize I'm out of line here."
"I'm heading out. I won't return home today."
If so, what is it that's beginning to stain my speech?
"Hang in there…"
Is it fatigue? A sense of obligation? Weakness?
"I have to hang in there!"
Come to think of it…
I was supposed to… stop telling myself to hang in there…
